summary: Vincent Eltschinger works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Lausanne, Fribourg, and Vienna (doctorate under Tom Tillemans), he held posts at Lausanne, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (directeur d’études from ~2015).

Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1993–1997). He held posts at CNRS (~1998–2012), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (2007), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2012).

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Bruno Dagens at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (HDR 2007), and has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, Seishi Karashima, and at Leiden and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (PhD 2012). He held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2021).
Vincenzo Vergiani is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raffaele Torella. He headed a Sanskrit manuscript research project at the University of Cambridge from ~2011 to 2016.
Virendra Kumar Varma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under traditional teachers Ramnath Dixit and Gopalchandra Mishra, and taught Kamala Prasad Tripathi.
Virendra Kumar Verma is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopalchandra Mishra, and taught Kamala Prasad Mishra.

Virendra Nath Misra was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961). He served as Director of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from ~1993 to 2000.

Vishva Bandhu was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Founder-Principal of Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921), Director at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College (1934), and worked at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1924–1973), directing it from ~1934 to 1973.
Vishwa Nath Pathak was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as a professor at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973–1978 and 1987).

Vishwanath Narayan Mandlik was an Indologist and historian educated at Elphinstone College (~1847–1851). He served as an examiner at the University of Mumbai and as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878).
Vishwanath Prasad Varma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, Kali Kinkar Datta, and Joachim Wach (1950).
Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz (MA supervisor until 2007), Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita.

Vladimir Minorsky was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and history. After studying at Moscow Imperial University and the Lazarev Institute, he held academic posts at INALCO (~1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (~1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov is a historian of Buddhism and religion. Educated at St. Petersburg University, Korea University, and Moscow State University, he taught at Kyung Hee University (1997–2000) and the University of Oslo (Associate Professor 2000, Professor 2006).

Vladimir Vyacheslavovich Balabushevich was a scholar in Indology and history. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).
Volkbert Näther is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (attested 1975) under the supervision of Claus Vogel.

Volker Caumanns works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hamburg (under David P. Jackson) and Munich (PhD under Franz-Karl Ehrhard). His posts include Munich (2006–2012), Lumbini International Research Institute (2012–2015), and Bern (attested 2019).

Volker Grabowsky specializes in history and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kiel, Chiang Mai, and Hamburg, he held posts at Passau, Laos, Münster (Professor 1999), and the University of Hamburg (Professor and department head from 2009).

Volker Zotz works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Vienna (~1975–1986) and a student of Anagarika Govinda, he held positions at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland, and the University of Luxembourg (~2006–2017).
